headword: {花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}
gloss: beauties of nature; the beauty of the natural world

definitions.gloss: beauties of nature; the beauty of the natural world; scenic beauty
definitions.explanation: A four-character idiom ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) referring to the beauty found in nature and the refined appreciation of it. Literally 'flowers, birds, wind, and moon' — four quintessential elements of natural beauty in East Asian aesthetics.

examples.japanese: {花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{愛|あい}する→愛する：01811_aisuru⟧。
examples.english: To love the beauties of nature.

examples.japanese: ⟦{俳句|はいく}→俳句：00083_haiku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧⟦{文学|ぶんがく}→文学：01505_bungaku⟧だ。
examples.english: Haiku is a literary form that celebrates the beauties of nature.

examples.japanese: ⟦{引退|いんたい}→引退：01848_intai⟧⟦したら→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{田舎|いなか}→田舎：01320_inaka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しみ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{暮|く}らしたい→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧。
examples.english: After retirement, I'd like to live in the countryside enjoying the beauties of nature.

notes:
A ⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧ (four-character idiom) representing the aesthetic appreciation of nature.

ETYMOLOGY:
{花|か} (flowers) + {鳥|ちょう} (birds) + {風|ふう} (wind) + {月|げつ} (moon) — four archetypal elements of natural beauty in East Asian culture.

- {花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{愛|め}でる→愛でる：12627_mederu⟧: to admire the beauties of nature
- {花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧: to compose poetry about nature

CULTURAL NOTE:
This concept is deeply rooted in Japanese and Chinese literary traditions. It represents the refined sensibility of finding beauty in the natural world — a central theme in haiku, waka poetry, ink painting, and tea ceremony aesthetics. The appreciation of {花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ} is considered a mark of cultural refinement.
